**Trace: browser GET `/file/users/{identifier}/avatar` → stored avatar data**

- `RegisterRoutes` (route `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` → `serveUserAvatar`) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`
- `serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168-210` (HTTP handler; reads `identifier` path param)
- `getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:714-717` (looks up the target user by username)
- `Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go:148-169` (checks the in-memory `userCache`, otherwise delegates to `ListUsers`)
- `Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go:136-146` (delegates to the underlying driver)
- `(*DB).ListUsers` (driver implementation, e.g. SQLite) — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:88-153` (issues the `SELECT ... FROM user WHERE ...` query against the `user` table, returning `AvatarURL` among other columns; equivalent implementations exist at `store/db/postgres/user.go` and `store/db/mysql/user.go`)
- Back in `serveUserAvatar`, `user.AvatarURL` (the data URI fetched from the row above) is parsed via `parseDataURI` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:196,736-750` — and the decoded image bytes are written to the response with `c.Blob(...)` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:209`.

Note: unlike memo attachments (which support LOCAL/S3/DB blob storage in the `attachment` table), user avatars in this codebase are stored inline as a base64 data URI in the `user.avatar_url` column itself — so the "data layer" hop terminates directly at the `user` table row rather than at separate attachment storage.
